evaluations.generated_requirements: FR-001: The mobile football app must be available for download and installation on both Android and iOS devices.
evaluations.feedback: This is only partially correct and is too narrow. The source states the app will be available for Android and iOS devices, but this requirement adds an unstated assumption about store discovery/download only. It also lacks completeness because it does not verify operability on both platforms after installation. The acceptance criteria use Given-When-Then format, but they are incomplete for the stated requirement and not sufficiently testable for platform support beyond app store presence.
evaluations.rewritten_requirement:
FR-001: The system shall provide the LiveFootball mobile application for both Android and iOS platforms.
User story: As a football fan, I want the app to be available on Android and iOS so that I can use it on my mobile device.
Acceptance criteria:
Given I use a supported Android device,
When I install and launch the LiveFootball app,
Then the app shall open and be usable on Android.
Given I use a supported iOS device,
When I install and launch the LiveFootball app,
Then the app shall open and be usable on iOS.

evaluations.generated_requirements: FR-002: The system must allow users to select their favorite teams and preferred sports channels to display a personalized news feed.
evaluations.feedback: This captures part of the personalization scope, but it is incomplete. The source says users can display current football news of favorite teams and select preferred sports channels individually. The requirement does not clarify that both filters may be applied independently or together, and it omits persistence of those preferences. Acceptance criteria are too vague because 'show current news related to my selected preferences' is not specific enough to verify behavior for favorite teams and channels separately.
evaluations.rewritten_requirement:
FR-002: The system shall allow users to select one or more favorite teams and one or more preferred sports channels, and shall use those selections to filter the football news shown in the app.
User story: As a user, I want to select favorite teams and preferred sports channels so that the news feed reflects my interests.
Acceptance criteria:
Given I am on the news preferences screen,
When I select one or more favorite teams and save my preferences,
Then the app shall display current news related to those teams.
Given I am on the news preferences screen,
When I select one or more preferred sports channels and save my preferences,
Then the app shall display current news from those channels.
Given I have selected favorite teams and preferred sports channels,
When I open the news feed,
Then the app shall show news matching my saved team and channel preferences.

evaluations.generated_requirements: FR-003: The app must provide a live ticker feature that displays real-time match results for users' favorite teams.
evaluations.feedback: This covers only one part of the live ticker scope. The source mentions an integrated live ticker module enabling retrieval and display of live data in real time, communication with the UI, and data retrieval via an external API/server. Restricting the requirement only to favorite teams omits the broader live ticker module behavior. Acceptance criteria are simplistic and do not verify continuous updates or real-time retrieval.
evaluations.rewritten_requirement:
FR-003: The system shall provide an integrated live ticker module that retrieves live match data from an external API and displays continuously updated match results in the user interface, including for the user's favorite teams.
User story: As a football fan, I want to follow live match results in real time so that I stay updated during matches.
Acceptance criteria:
Given a match is in progress and live data is available from the external API,
When I open the live ticker screen,
Then the app shall display the current match data in the user interface.
Given a match is in progress and new live data is received from the external API,
When the live ticker screen is open,
Then the displayed match data shall update to reflect the latest available result.
Given I have selected favorite teams,
When one of my favorite teams is playing,
Then the live ticker shall include that team's live match data.

evaluations.generated_requirements: FR-004: The app must offer coverage and display information for all major football leagues and competitions, both national and international.
evaluations.feedback: This is not faithful to the source. The original document says 'all leagues and competitions, both national and international,' not 'all major.' 'Major' reduces scope and introduces ambiguity. Acceptance criteria are also weak because 'any available option' avoids the core completeness issue. This requirement fails completeness and precision.
evaluations.rewritten_requirement:
FR-004: The system shall provide coverage and display information for football leagues and competitions at national and international levels.
User story: As a user, I want access to national and international leagues and competitions so that I can follow the football competitions that interest me.
Acceptance criteria:
Given I navigate to the leagues and competitions section,
When I browse the available competitions,
Then the app shall present both national and international football competitions.
Given I select a listed league or competition,
When its detail view opens,
Then the app shall display information for that league or competition.

evaluations.generated_requirements: FR-005: The system must provide detailed information and statistics about teams and players at all times.
evaluations.feedback: This is partially aligned, but it introduces 'statistics' and 'biographical info' that are not explicitly stated in the source. While plausible, they are assumptions. The source only guarantees detailed team and player information at any time. Acceptance criteria therefore test unstated content instead of traceable scope. The requirement should stay within the source wording unless decomposed with agreed definitions.
evaluations.rewritten_requirement:
FR-005: The system shall provide users with detailed information about teams and players and make that information accessible at any time within the app.
User story: As a user, I want to access detailed team and player information so that I can view football information whenever I need it.
Acceptance criteria:
Given I select a team in the app,
When the team details screen opens,
Then the app shall display detailed information for that team.
Given I select a player in the app,
When the player details screen opens,
Then the app shall display detailed information for that player.
Given the app is operational,
When I navigate to a team or player details screen,
Then the information shall be available to view.

evaluations.generated_requirements: FR-006: The app must integrate live stream links from providers such as DAZN or Sky Sport, displaying them to users when the live broadcast has begun and rights are available.
evaluations.feedback: This is largely traceable to the source and uses valid BDD acceptance criteria. However, it would be stronger if it explicitly stated that links are shown directly in the app and that the condition includes both broadcast start and rights validation for the user's country. It narrowly passes because the core behavior is represented and testable.
evaluations.rewritten_requirement:
FR-006: The system shall integrate live stream links from broadcast providers such as DAZN or Sky Sport and display those links directly in the app only after the live broadcast has started and broadcast rights are valid for the user's country.
User story: As a football fan, I want to access live stream links in the app when they become legally available so that I can watch live football from authorized providers.
Acceptance criteria:
Given a match has an associated stream provider and the broadcast rights are valid for my country,
When the live broadcast starts,
Then the app shall display the live stream link directly in the app.
Given a match has not yet started,
When I view the match in the app,
Then the live stream link shall not be displayed.

evaluations.generated_requirements: FR-007: The app must ensure live stream links are displayed only when the transmission rights are fulfilled for the user's country.
evaluations.feedback: This overlaps heavily with FR-006 and should not be a separate independent story in its current form because it is not sufficiently independent under INVEST. It also misses the negative case explicitly: links must not be shown when rights are not fulfilled. Acceptance criteria only cover the positive case and do not test withholding unavailable content. This creates duplication and incomplete coverage.
evaluations.rewritten_requirement:
FR-007: The system shall restrict display of live stream links based on broadcast rights for the user's country and shall hide stream links when rights are not valid in that country.
User story: As a user, I want to see only stream links that are legally available in my country so that I do not encounter inaccessible or unauthorized content.
Acceptance criteria:
Given a live match has broadcast rights valid for my country,
When I open the match details,
Then the app shall display the live stream link.
Given a live match does not have broadcast rights valid for my country,
When I open the match details,
Then the app shall not display any live stream link for that match.

evaluations.generated_requirements: FR-008: The system must allow users to enable notifications for current events regarding their favorite teams.
evaluations.feedback: This is incomplete. The source explicitly mentions notifications for news or results of favorite teams and that notifications are sent when the notification function is activated. 'Current events' is vague and weakens traceability. Acceptance criteria do not distinguish notification types or activation state clearly enough. The requirement should cover enabling notifications and receiving notifications for favorite-team news and results.
evaluations.rewritten_requirement:
FR-008: The system shall allow users to activate notifications and receive notifications about news and match results related to their favorite teams.
User story: As a user, I want to receive notifications about news and results for my favorite teams so that I stay informed in real time.
Acceptance criteria:
Given I have selected one or more favorite teams and enabled notifications,
When a news item related to one of my favorite teams is published,
Then the app shall send me a notification about that news item.
Given I have selected one or more favorite teams and enabled notifications,
When a result update occurs for one of my favorite teams,
Then the app shall send me a notification about that result.
Given notifications are disabled,
When a news item or result update occurs for one of my favorite teams,
Then the app shall not send me a notification.

evaluations.generated_requirements: FR-009: The system must allow users to share news articles and game reports via social media directly from the app.
evaluations.feedback: This is aligned with the source and the BDD structure is acceptable. It would be stronger if it specified that sharing is initiated from within the app and opens available social targets on the device, but the current wording is sufficiently testable and in scope.
evaluations.rewritten_requirement:
FR-009: The system shall allow users to share news articles and game reports directly from the app via social media applications available on the user's device.
User story: As a user, I want to share news articles and game reports from the app so that I can post them on social media.
Acceptance criteria:
Given I am viewing a news article or game report in the app,
When I tap the share option,
Then the app shall present available social media sharing options on my device.
Given I select a social media sharing option,
When I confirm the share action,
Then the selected content shall be passed to that social media application for posting.

evaluations.generated_requirements: FR-010: The registration and login process must be straightforward and allow users to complete signup or login directly at app startup.
evaluations.feedback: The source supports direct registration/login at startup, but 'straightforward' and 'a few straightforward steps' are subjective and not testable. The requirement lacks concrete functional behavior, such as presenting registration and login options at startup and allowing completion there. It fails quality/testability.
evaluations.rewritten_requirement:
FR-010: The system shall present registration and login options at app startup and allow users to complete account registration or login from the startup flow.
User story: As a user, I want to register or log in when the app starts so that I can access personalized features immediately.
Acceptance criteria:
Given I launch the app,
When the startup screen is displayed,
Then the app shall provide options to register and to log in.
Given I select the registration option at startup,
When I submit valid registration data,
Then the app shall create my account and allow me to proceed.
Given I select the login option at startup,
When I submit valid login credentials,
Then the app shall authenticate me and allow me to proceed.

evaluations.generated_requirements: FR-011: The system must allow users to personalize the app by following preferred clubs and configuring the app interface to their preferences.
evaluations.feedback: This requirement improperly merges two distinct concepts: following favorite clubs and configuring the app via additional modules/interface connections. The source also says additional modules allow users to individually configure the app and connect their own interface to the user interface, which is not captured clearly here. 'Adjust the interface' is vague, and the acceptance criteria are not specific enough to test what configuration means. This fails INVEST due to combining multiple features ambiguously.
evaluations.rewritten_requirement:
FR-011: The system shall allow users to follow favorite clubs for personalization purposes.
User story: As a user, I want to follow my favorite clubs so that the app can personalize content for me.
Acceptance criteria:
Given I am viewing club personalization options,
When I select one or more clubs as favorites and save my changes,
Then the app shall store those clubs as my favorites.
Given I have saved favorite clubs,
When I use the app,
Then personalized features shall use those favorite clubs.

FR-012: The system shall provide configuration modules that users can access through the user interface to individually configure app settings.
User story: As a user, I want to configure the app through available modules so that the app experience can be adapted to my preferences.
Acceptance criteria:
Given configuration modules are available in the app,
When I open a configuration module through the user interface,
Then I shall be able to view and modify the settings exposed by that module.
Given I save a configuration change in a module,
When I return to the relevant area of the app,
Then the app shall apply the saved configuration.

evaluations.generated_requirements: NFR-001: The app must load fully and be ready for use within a maximum of two seconds after starting, on supported devices.
evaluations.feedback: This accurately reflects the source and is testable. The BDD format is present. It would be stronger if startup conditions were defined more precisely, such as cold start and supported device/network conditions, but the requirement is still acceptable.
evaluations.rewritten_requirement:
NFR-001: The system shall complete app startup and be ready for user interaction within 2 seconds of launch on supported Android and iOS devices.
User story: As a mobile user, I want the app to start quickly so that I can access features without delay.
Acceptance criteria:
Given the app is installed on a supported device,
When I launch the app,
Then the app shall be ready for user interaction within 2 seconds.

evaluations.generated_requirements: NFR-002: All app modules and the user interface must remain consistent in their design and functionality, even if the external server is updated.
evaluations.feedback: This is loosely traceable but too subjective. 'Consistent in their design and functionality' and 'remain unchanged' are vague. The source says modules and UI are fixed components of the app and remain consistent even with external server updates. The requirement should express that server-side updates must not alter client module availability or UI structure unexpectedly. Current acceptance criteria are not measurable enough.
evaluations.rewritten_requirement:
NFR-002: External server updates shall not change the availability of client-side app modules or break the defined user interface structure in released app versions.
User story: As a user, I want the app's core interface and modules to remain stable after server updates so that I can continue using the app without disruption.
Acceptance criteria:
Given a released version of the app is connected to an updated external server,
When I open the app and navigate through its core modules,
Then the same client-side modules shall remain accessible.
Given a released version of the app is connected to an updated external server,
When I use the core user interface flows,
Then the user interface structure shall continue to function without breaking due to the server update.

evaluations.generated_requirements: NFR-003: The app must function reliably and maintain usability even under conditions of limited network coverage.
evaluations.feedback: This is in scope but too vague. 'Core app features' and 'function as expected' are not measurable. The source also separately states the app remains usable offline if connection is temporarily lost. This requirement should be constrained to degraded-network behavior without duplicating offline behavior. As written, it is not sufficiently testable.
evaluations.rewritten_requirement:
NFR-003: The system shall continue to provide usable access to app screens and non-live content under limited network coverage, with degraded network conditions not causing the app to become unusable.
User story: As a user in a low-connectivity area, I want the app to remain usable so that I can still access information.
Acceptance criteria:
Given the device has limited network coverage,
When I navigate through the app,
Then the app shall continue to open screens and display any available cached or previously retrieved content.
Given the device has limited network coverage,
When live data cannot be refreshed immediately,
Then the app shall remain responsive and shall not crash or block user navigation.

evaluations.generated_requirements: NFR-004: The app must remain usable offline, allowing access to previously loaded data, even if network connectivity is temporarily lost.
evaluations.feedback: This is a reasonable interpretation of the source and is testable. It would be improved by explicitly stating that offline usability is for previously loaded or cached information because not all features can logically work offline, but the current wording already hints at that.
evaluations.rewritten_requirement:
NFR-004: The system shall remain usable during temporary loss of network connectivity and shall allow access to previously loaded data while offline.
User story: As a user, I want to continue using the app when my connection is lost so that I can still access available information.
Acceptance criteria:
Given I have previously loaded content in the app,
When the device loses network connectivity,
Then I shall still be able to open the app and view that previously loaded content.
Given the device is offline,
When I navigate within the app,
Then the app shall remain usable without crashing.

evaluations.generated_requirements: NFR-005: The app must be able to serve up to 100,000 users simultaneously during high-traffic periods such as match days without any noticeable performance loss.
evaluations.feedback: This is close to the source, but 'noticeable performance loss' is subjective and not measurable. The source says 'without performance loss,' which is itself difficult, but the rewritten requirement should operationalize it using measurable service-level criteria. Acceptance criteria currently remain vague and therefore fail quality/testability.
evaluations.rewritten_requirement:
NFR-005: The system shall support at least 100,000 concurrent users during peak periods such as match days while maintaining defined response-time and availability targets.
User story: As an operator, I want the app to support peak match-day traffic so that users can continue using the service reliably.
Acceptance criteria:
Given a load test simulates 100,000 concurrent users,
When the system is under peak load,
Then the service shall remain available to users.
Given a load test simulates 100,000 concurrent users,
When users perform supported app actions,
Then the measured response times shall remain within the project's defined performance thresholds.

evaluations.generated_requirements: NFR-006: The app must undergo thorough testing and support processes before release to detect and resolve any malfunctions early.
evaluations.feedback: This is not a good product requirement in its current form; it is a process statement rather than a system requirement. It also uses vague terms like 'thorough' and 'stable.' While the source mentions testing and support before release, the generated item lacks measurable release criteria. Acceptance criteria are not sufficiently objective. It should be reframed as a release quality gate if included at all.
evaluations.rewritten_requirement:
NFR-006: Before each production release, the product shall pass a defined pre-release test and support process in which all critical defects are resolved or formally accepted.
User story: As a release manager, I want each release to pass pre-release quality checks so that major malfunctions are identified before users receive the app.
Acceptance criteria:
Given a release candidate is prepared for production,
When the defined pre-release test process is completed,
Then no open critical defects shall remain unless formally approved for release.
Given a defect is identified during pre-release validation,
When the defect severity is classified as critical,
Then the release shall not proceed until the defect is resolved or formally accepted through the release process.

evaluations.generated_requirements: NFR-007: All processing of users' personal data must be performed in compliance with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR).
evaluations.feedback: This is traceable but too broad and legally loaded to be testable as written. GDPR compliance should be decomposed into implementable requirements such as consent, lawful processing, data subject rights, and data minimization. The current acceptance criterion merely restates the requirement and is not sufficient BDD validation. As written, it fails testability.
evaluations.rewritten_requirement:
NFR-007: The system shall process users' personal data in accordance with GDPR requirements applicable to the app's operation.
User story: As a user, I want my personal data to be handled in a GDPR-compliant manner so that my privacy rights are protected.
Acceptance criteria:
Given the app requests personal data from a user,
When the data is collected,
Then the app shall present the applicable privacy information required for that processing.
Given a user has not provided required consent for an optional data-processing activity,
When the app attempts that optional processing,
Then the app shall not process the user's personal data for that activity.
Given a user account contains personal data,
When the system stores or uses that data,
Then the processing shall follow the app's defined GDPR compliance rules and controls.
